before.content:
<!-- layout: title; theme: briefing; design: v1 -->
# The intake pilot

A shorter review cycle, with an unanswered quality question. [1][2]

---

<!-- layout: composed -->
<!-- scene:  -->
## The pilot measured time; quality remains unknown [1][2]

In this synthetic intake pilot, median review time was 40 hours before the pilot and 16 hours during the pilot. The observation covered two teams over eight weeks. These are training data, not actual organizational results. [1]

The two-team intake pilot did not measure review quality or error rates. A faster review cannot establish a quality improvement. The sample does not establish an effect in other teams. [2]

findings.problem: Body text is 18.2px; the body floor is 22px.
findings.correction: Allocate more room and increase type; keep values and qualifications intact.

findings.problem: The slide's essential limitation (no quality or error-rate measurement; cannot infer a quality improvement; no cross-team effect) is set at 18.25 pt, below the 22 pt body minimum, and visibly smaller than the 23.36 pt result column. The qualification the decision hinges on is the weakest text on the slide.
findings.correction: Set this paragraph to at least 22 pt, matching the result column's body size, and rebalance the two columns so the limitation reads at comparable weight to the time result. Keep the text and the [2] marker unchanged.

findings.problem: The result column is only about 205 px wide, so the paragraph wraps to one or two words per line over roughly 20 lines, creating a tall, slow-to-read ladder of text.
findings.correction: Widen this column to a readable measure (roughly 45-60 characters per line) and give the shorter limitation column less width, so neither column runs as a narrow ladder. Keep all text and citation markers.

findings.problem: The headline states what was measured, but the actual result (40 hours before, 16 hours during) is buried mid-paragraph in running text; the slide's main finding has no visual anchor for a scanning decision-maker.
findings.correction: Pull the two medians into a prominent stat line or lead element above the supporting sentence, leaving the surrounding text and its [1] marker intact.

attemptFindings.problem: The two citation markers in the heading collide: the closing bracket of [1] and the opening bracket of [2] overlap, rendering as a mangled glyph that reads like a broken character rather than two separate markers. This makes the heading's sourcing unreadable.
attemptFindings.correction: Keep both markers but add horizontal space between them (e.g., a thin space or increased letter/word spacing on the superscript run) so they render as two clearly distinct markers [1] [2] without overlapping.
